tooltip.title: Therapeutic Modalities
tooltip.markdown: Treatment aims to suppress autoantibody production and inflammation to stop blistering and promote healing.

tooltip.title: Corticosteroids
tooltip.markdown: The mainstay of initial therapy for most autoimmune bullous diseases to gain rapid control of inflammation.

tooltip.title: High-Potency Topical Steroids
tooltip.markdown: (e.g., Clobetasol) A first-line, preferred treatment for localized or even generalized Bullous Pemphigoid, as it has fewer systemic side effects than oral steroids.

tooltip.title: Systemic Steroids
tooltip.markdown: (e.g., Prednisone) Required for most cases of Pemphigus and severe cases of other bullous diseases to induce remission.

tooltip.title: Conventional Immunosuppressants ("Steroid-Sparing" Agents)
tooltip.markdown: Added to systemic steroids to allow for dose reduction and long-term maintenance, minimizing steroid toxicity.

tooltip.title: Antimetabolites
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Mycophenolate Mofetil (MMF)**
-   **Azathioprine**
-   Both are commonly used as first-line steroid-sparing agents in Pemphigus and Pemphigoid.

tooltip.title: Dapsone
tooltip.markdown: A sulfone antibiotic with potent anti-neutrophilic effects. It is the absolute first-line treatment for Dermatitis Herpetiformis and Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis.

tooltip.title: Tetracyclines & Nicotinamide
tooltip.markdown: (e.g., Doxycycline, Minocycline) A well-tolerated combination with anti-inflammatory properties, often used for milder Bullous Pemphigoid.

tooltip.title: Biologic & Targeted Therapies
tooltip.markdown: Highly specific agents for refractory or severe disease.

tooltip.title: Rituximab
tooltip.markdown: A monoclonal antibody that depletes B-cells (the source of autoantibodies). Now a first-line agent, along with steroids, for moderate-to-severe Pemphigus.

tooltip.title: Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG)
tooltip.markdown: A pool of human antibodies thought to work by neutralizing pathogenic autoantibodies. Used for severe, refractory disease.

tooltip.title: Other Targeted Therapies
tooltip.markdown: Includes agents like Dupilumab and Omalizumab for Bullous Pemphigoid.
